newsitem.title: SPAIN: BBV still hungry for Latin American banks.
newsitem.headline: BBV still hungry for Latin American banks.

text.p: Despite gobbling up stakes in several Latin American banks in 1996, Spain's second-largest bank, Banco Bilbao Vizcaya is hungry for more, with both acquisitions and new branches on the menu.
"We want to complete our presence and constitute our group in Latin America," said Jose Ignacio Goirigolzarri, who handles Latin America for the bank.
BBV reported earnings of 58.11 billion pesetas in the first half of the year, a rise of 25.9 percent from a year ago.
Profits from its Latin American operations provided 30 percent of its total profit, a decisive contribution, said bank chairman Emilio Ybarra.
"Latin America is the star in the presentation of results," Goirigolzarri said.

BBV has been capitalising on its new investments in Latin America. It is taking advantage of high growth and fat margins to compensate for falling domestic margins and for the potential loss of business with the euro's launch set for 1999.

This year, after an aggressive 1996 shopping spree, BBV has acquired 40 percent of Provincial in Venezuela and 71.7 percent of Credito Argentino. As of May, BBV had assets of 3.9 trillion pesetas and 1,150 offices in Latin America.
BBV now plans to strengthen its current investments and does not rule out eventual purchases in Chile and Brazil.
"It is clear that BBV is interested in those markets," Goirigolzarri said.
But he said that so far BBV had found no candidates that fit its strategy.
"In Chile, the banks we are looking at are very expensive and we are still looking at Brazil as well," he said.

Spanish rival Santander just made a key Brazilian purchase, while BBV has no presence in Latin America's biggest banking market. Another domestic competitor, Banco Central Hispano, is Chile's biggest banker.
BBV said it will also present a bid soon in the imminent Mexican tender for bank Banpais.
Throughout Latin America, the group plans to open new offices to increase market share, provide better customer service and improve market efficiency.
"We are going to increase our market share by opening more offices," Goirigolzarri said.
